items.title: A Noetherian regular ring of finite dimension is a strong generator for its perfect complexes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a Noetherian regular ring R of finite dimension d is a strong generator for the full subcategory of perfect objects of D(R) (source lines 20819-20824). The proof is a genuine induction on the projective dimension bound, using the characterisation of perfect objects as bounded complexes with finite cohomology and the definition of generation in a bounded number of steps. It first records that every finite R-module has projective dimension at most d, so that d + 1 is the generation bound, then proves by induction on i that if every H^n(K) has projective dimension at most i then K lies in the i + 1-fold generated subcategory of R (proof lines 20832-20840). The base case i = 0 uses that projective cohomology modules have vanishing higher Ext between them, so that K splits as the direct sum of the shifts of its cohomology, and each finite projective module is a summand of a sum of copies of R (proof lines 20843-20852). The induction step is the substantive part: it picks a surjection from a finite free module onto each cohomology module, lifts these to maps F^n[-n] -> K in the derived category, takes the associated distinguished triangle K' -> bigoplus F^n[-n] -> K -> K'[1], reads off the short exact sequences 0 -> H^n(K') -> F^n -> H^n(K) -> 0, and uses the projective-dimension subadditivity to bound the projective dimension of H^n(K') by max(0, i), so that K' lies in the i+1-fold generated subcategory and hence K lies in the i+2-fold one (proof lines 20855-20879). The non-routine content is the bookkeeping of the generation index through the distinguished triangle, together with the projective-dimension drop that makes the induction go through.
